newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares close mixed in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares close mixed in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Indian share prices ended mixed in lethargic trade at major bourses on Friday, with little action seen in blue-chips ahead of the weekend, dealers said.

Trading activity focussed on State Bank of India shares after the company announced a 179 percent jump in 1996/97 (April-March) net profit to 6.41 billion rupees just after close of trade on Thursday.
"Dull trade was the highlight of the day's action contrary to expectations of fireworks taking place after better results announced by SBI," a dealer at a local brokerage said.
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) ended 19.48 points, or 0.68 percent, down at 2,890.50.

SBI closed 2.0 rupees up at 218.25 at the BSE in volumes of over 4.7 million shares. With foreign funds' holdings reaching the 20 percent limit in the stock, little investment buying in SBI is seen taking place, traders said.
Market-favourite SBI met market expectations after showing a smart rise in its first half net profit, but traders said the initial cheer after the good results had subsided.
"Surprisingly, a lot of action expected in the SBI counter failed to come up," the dealer added.
After close of trade, state-run Bharat Heavy Electronics Ltd (BHEL) said its first half 1996/97 net profit rose 41 percent to 687.2 million rupees against 486.8 million a year ago.

BHEL rose 5.0 rupees to 195.50 rupees, ITC 2.75 to 279.75, Bajaj Auto 18.50 to 844.0, MTNL 1.0 to 215.50 and M&M 7.25 to 289.25. Reliance shares were unchanged at 180.75. TISCO fell 0.75 to 153.25, ACC 7.25 to 1,002.75.
"There were very few participants in the market," said Amit Sethi of Delhi brokers Vashisht Securities. The National Stock Exchange (NSE) index gained 4.85 points to 830.32.
